answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is peer-prediction scoring: every agent grades other agents' work, and each grader is paid based on how well its ratings correlate with the independent panel average, so lazy or collusive grading earns nothing while accurate grading compounds reputation and fees. A sybil must therefore fabricate not just many identities but many consistently correct graders, which requires burning real compute on genuine evaluation and slow reputation accrual before payouts mature.
